name: Modular grid
summary: A page or screen divided into equal columns and rows; each element fits a cell or a block of cells, so that the whole layout repeats one measure.
how: Divide the page into 4 to 12 equal columns with a gutter of 1/10 to 1/5 of a column width.
Cut the page into rows of the same module height; align each image and text block to the lines.
Set text on a baseline grid of one line height, and use 1 to 2 type sizes for each level.
Scale an image by a whole number of modules.

origin.note: Josef Mueller-Brockmann and the journal Neue Grafik (1958) spread the modular grid for posters and print.

adoptions.via: Otl Aicher builds the corporate design of Lufthansa on a fixed grid of marks, type and colour.
Unimark issues the New York City Transit Graphics Standards Manual, with sign grids for the whole system.
Windows Phone 7 builds its start screen from square and wide live tiles on one grid.
Bootstrap 2.0 ships a 12 column fluid grid for web pages.
Interfaces that follow the Braun products of Dieter Rams put each control in one cell of a strict grid.

sources.title: Josef Mueller-Brockmann, Grid Systems in Graphic Design (Niggli, 1981)
